meta_description: Post-Quantum Cryptography Migration from Dataq Software: scope, delivery pattern, platforms and committed outcomes.

blocks.x: Buyers rarely need another definition of post-quantum cryptography migration. They need to know what ships first, what it touches and how value is proven. That is what this page carries: Beat the harvest-now-decrypt-later clock — cryptographic inventory to PQC cutover.

PQC migration is a decade-long program compressed into this decade: NIST standards (ML-KEM, ML-DSA, SLH-DSA) are published, regulators are turning attention to long-lived secrets, and adversaries are already harvesting. We run the full program: cryptographic discovery (code, libraries, appliances, certificates, protocols — including the shadow crypto nobody documented), risk ranking by exposure horizon, remediation sequencing, and crypto-agility architecture so the next migration is a config change, not another decade.

Cutover is engineering, not memo: hybrid key establishment during transition periods, protocol and library upgrades with performance testing, HSM and smartcard lifecycle, vendor attestation tracking, and certificate authority planning. For financial-sector clients we align with emerging supervisory expectations; for long-lived-data holders (health, government, defense-adjacent) we prioritize by data sensitivity and retention horizon.

The sectors where Post-Quantum Cryptography Migration currently runs: Banking & Financial Services, Public Sector & Government, Healthcare & Life Sciences, Energy & Utilities. Each engagement anchors to one named metric in that sector's own language.
What ships, in the order it ships:
